boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Johns Hopkins rituals, recurring celebrations, student customs, and ceremonial objects—from painting Jay to waiting until graduation to step on the Gilman seal.

cards.title: Open the Year with a Blue Jay Tailgate
cards.subtitle: An academic-and-athletic kickoff with rides, games, music, and campus groups
cards.notes: Start the year at the university-wide tailgate; explore the games, photo booth, giveaways, and tables for campus resources.
cards.short_summary: Hopkins begins its academic and athletic calendars with a campus-wide celebration built around Blue Jay community life.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins Student Affairs says Blue Jay Opening Day kicks off the academic and athletic years with rides, games, a photo booth, a DJ, giveaways, and campus resources.
cards.access_notes: The cited page documents the recurring event but does not provide a current date, venue, admission rule, or public-access policy; verify the event listing before attending.

cards.title: Turn Fall into Hoptoberfest
cards.subtitle: A Hopkins fall tradition that has included pumpkins, crafts, music, and activities
cards.notes: Check the current Hoptoberfest schedule, then choose among the seasonal activities rather than assuming every past feature will return.
cards.short_summary: Hopkins marks early fall with a named annual celebration whose programming changes from year to year.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins Student Affairs identifies Hoptoberfest as an annual fall tradition featuring music, activities, and food, with past programs including a pumpkin patch, crafts, screenings, and a fun run.
cards.access_notes: The official traditions page does not list current dates, venue, admission requirements, or attendee eligibility; consult the current campus event notice.

cards.title: Count Down to the Quad Lights
cards.subtitle: The president flips a ceremonial switch as Hopkins closes the fall term in lights
cards.notes: Arrive before the countdown to see student performances and illuminated art; confirm the year's quad and fireworks plan before going.
cards.short_summary: The community gathers annually for a presidential countdown that switches on thousands of campus lights.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins Student Affairs says the community gathers yearly for Lighting of the Quads, where President Daniels leads a countdown before a ceremonial switch illuminates thousands of lights and a fireworks display.
cards.access_notes: Location and programming can change because of campus conditions; use the current university event announcement for the date, designated viewing area, and access rules.

cards.title: Watch Campus Become Spring Fair
cards.subtitle: An annual Hopkins festival of crafts, games, contests, food, and live music
cards.notes: Review the current fair program and campus layout, then plan around the named stages, vendors, games, and activities you want to see.
cards.short_summary: Once each year, Spring Fair converts the university grounds into a multi-part festival with student-life programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins Student Affairs calls Spring Fair a Johns Hopkins tradition held once a year and documents arts and crafts, games, contests, food, and live music among its features.
cards.access_notes: The traditions page does not establish current dates, admission, individual activity costs, or public access; consult the current Spring Fair program.

cards.title: Give Jay a New Coat of Paint
cards.subtitle: Students repaint the Blue Jay statue with messages, art, and event announcements
cards.notes: Photograph Jay's current design or join a thoughtful repaint with friends; keep the work respectful and follow any current campus guidance.
cards.short_summary: A continually changing Blue Jay statue serves as Hopkins' student-painted canvas for expression and announcements.
cards.evidence_claim: A Johns Hopkins Admissions student-life article calls painting Jay a Hopkins tradition and states that all students may spray-paint the statue to share creative messages, advertisements, or awareness campaigns.
cards.access_notes: The source documents student participation but gives no hours or current paint-supply rules; follow posted university guidance and do not paint surrounding property.

cards.title: Design a Class Identity in Cloth
cards.subtitle: Incoming students create a banner intended to represent their class in perpetuity
cards.notes: Look for the incoming-class design call, submit through its official process, or view original banners during Alumni Weekend on Decker Quad.
cards.short_summary: Every incoming undergraduate class contributes a student-designed banner to a Hopkins tradition dating to 1881.
cards.evidence_claim: The Johns Hopkins Alumni Association says the Class Banner Competition dates to 1881, challenges each incoming class to design a permanent representative banner, and displays original banners during Alumni Weekend.
cards.access_notes: Competition eligibility and deadlines are not stated on the cited page. Banner viewing during Alumni Weekend depends on that event's current schedule and access rules.

cards.title: Follow the Mace into Commencement
cards.subtitle: A 40-inch ebony-and-silver staff leads the university's ceremonial procession
cards.notes: During Convocation or Commencement, watch for the chief marshal carrying the symbol-covered mace at the head of the procession.
cards.short_summary: Hopkins formal ceremonies begin behind an ebony staff adorned with silver symbols of scholarship and cultural development.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins reports that its ceremonial mace dates to 1954, appears at Convocation, and is carried by the Commencement chief marshal while leading the procession of dignitaries.
cards.access_notes: The mace is observed as part of formal university ceremonies; access depends on the applicable Convocation or Commencement invitation and venue rules.

cards.title: Bring Evergreen's Chair Back for One Day
cards.subtitle: A turn-of-the-century ceremonial chair returns to campus for Commencement
cards.notes: At Commencement, spot the triangular replica chair transported from Evergreen Museum and Library for the university president's use.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive wooden chair spends most of the year at Evergreen, then makes an annual ceremonial journey to Hopkins.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins says the President's Chair normally remains at Evergreen Museum and Library but is brought to campus once each year for the university president to sit in during Commencement.
cards.access_notes: View the chair from authorized audience areas during Commencement; ceremony admission and venue access are governed by current university instructions.

cards.title: Save the Gilman Seal for Graduation
cards.subtitle: Campus lore warns students away from the floor seal until their degrees are secure
cards.notes: Walk around the foyer seal while enrolled, then pose on it only after graduating if you want to play along with the Hopkins superstition.
cards.short_summary: Hopkins lore turns one floor medallion into a four-year exercise in careful foot placement—and a post-graduation photo stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Johns Hopkins documents the legend that prospective students who step on the Gilman seal will not be admitted and current students will not graduate, while noting that graduates step or dance on it afterward.
cards.access_notes: The seal is inside Gilman Hall. Enter only when the building is open to you, keep circulation paths clear, and follow all posted building rules.

cards.title: Make the Crab Wave at Lacrosse
cards.subtitle: A Hopkins game-day gesture shaped for Baltimore
cards.notes: At a Blue Jays lacrosse game, watch the student section for the crab wave and join only from your seat without blocking anyone's view.
cards.short_summary: Hopkins students add a Baltimore-specific hand gesture to the rituals surrounding Blue Jays lacrosse.
cards.evidence_claim: The Johns Hopkins News-Letter's 2026 sesquicentennial student bucket list places doing the crab wave at a lacrosse game in its Hopkins school-spirit section.
cards.source_title: The Hopkins sesquicentennial senior bucket list: 150 things to do before graduating
cards.access_notes: Attend only a scheduled game for which you have valid access; ticket requirements and venue policies vary by event and are not established by this source.
